subject.title: Memory system: Cannot delete stale memories, conflicting entries persist

question: Should OpenClaw fix this issue now by exposing a model-visible exact deletion selector from `memory_recall`, or should all deletion/replacement semantics wait for the broader Memory MVP lifecycle contract?
rationale: Source proves the recall-to-forget selector gap, but the issue also asks for replacement/deprecation semantics that affect durable memory state and plugin API behavior.

options.title: Narrow recall selector first
options.body: Add a safe visible UUID or equivalent deletion handle to `memory_recall`, keep UUID validation in `memory_forget`, and leave replacement/deprecation for the Memory MVP trackers.

options.title: Wait for lifecycle contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as a concrete symptom but defer implementation until review/edit/forget/tombstone/conflict semantics are designed together.

options.title: Fold into Memory MVP only
options.body: Close or retitle this after explicitly preserving the recall-to-forget symptom in the broader lifecycle/write-resolution issues.

recommendation.title: Narrow recall selector first
recommendation.body: Add a safe visible UUID or equivalent deletion handle to `memory_recall`, keep UUID validation in `memory_forget`, and leave replacement/deprecation for the Memory MVP trackers.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage and current memory-lancedb integration history make this the best available owner for choosing the immediate selector versus lifecycle-contract path.
